Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Church life

censer noun

also thurible, incense burner

classical

Cic. Verr. 2.4.46 (Lewis & Short)
Liv. 29.14.13 (Lewis & Short)
M-O s.v. incense burner, censer, thurible

tūribulum, tūribulī n.

noun, second declension

censer, thurible

Also spelled thūribulum, as in the Vulgate. The same vessel in both churches; the Orthodox censer has little bells on its chains.

Other words

  • thȳmiāmatērium, thȳmiāmatēriī n. — a censer

    noun, second declension · also used · late Latin · Vulg. Jer. 52.19 (Lewis & Short)

    From thȳmiāma, incense. Egeria calls the censers carried into the Anastasis before the Gospel by a related Greek name (24.10).

Examples

  • Et alius angelus vēnit, et stetit ante altāre habēns thūribulum aureum

    And another angel came and stood before the altar, holding a golden censerVulg. Apoc. 8.3

See also incense, deacon, altar.

SourcesLewis & Short: turibulum · Lewis & Short: thymiamaterium

Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. incense burner, censer, thurible.
